Article Title: Day 12 of Jharkhand students' protest: Hemant Soren says govt taking exam row 'very seriously'
Article Text:
Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren

NEW DELHI: Jharkhand chief minister Hemant Soren on Wednesday said the state government was treating allegations of irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) with "utmost seriousness and sensitivity," assuring students that justice would be delivered within the constitutional and legal framework.Soren's remarks marked his first public response since students launched protests over alleged paper leaks and irregularities in recruitment examinations."This is a sensitive government that believes in delivering justice. Whenever we take up an issue, we remain committed to resolving it. Our young people will certainly get justice within the ambit of the Constitution and the law," Soren said while speaking to reporters after a programme in Ramgarh district's Nemra village on the first death anniversary of Dishom Guru Shibu Soren."I cannot tear open my chest to show how serious we are, but the government is taking this matter very seriously. This government has eyes, ears and sensitivity. Whatever is appropriate and in the interest of students, the state government will decide accordingly," he added.The chief minister said investigations into the allegations were underway and that the government would take a decision after receiving reports from the agencies probing the matter."We are waiting for the findings and conclusions of the investigating agencies. The people of the state will soon be informed in detail about the matter. Students will receive full support in accordance with constitutional and legal provisions," he said.Soren said the government was closely monitoring developments and that administrative processes were continuing at all levels. He added that the probe agencies were actively investigating the allegations and that the government's final decision would be announced after all facts and findings were available.Meanwhile, students protesting at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium in Ranchi entered the 12th day of their agitation on Wednesday. They are demanding cancellation of the 14th JPSC Combined Civil Services Preliminary Examination, a CBI and ED probe into alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC recruitment examinations, disclosure of OMR sheets, main examination answer scripts and category-wise cut-off marks, blacklisting of controversial examination agencies, and comprehensive reforms in the state's recruitment bodies.
Article Summary: Jharkhand chief minister Hemant Soren said the state government was treating allegations of irregularities with "utmost seriousness and sensitivity" Soren's remarks marked his first public response since students launched protests over alleged paper leaks and irregularities in recruitment examinations. The chief minister said investigations into the allegations were underway.

Article Title: Govt distances itself from Hasina event but Dhaka not convinced
Article Text:
India has firmly denied any role in Sheikh Hasina's forthcoming media address, while Dhaka expresses skepticism, worried that the address may jeopardize diplomatic ties. Meanwhile, Bangladesh's Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has received an invitation to the Brics summit from India, but he may encounter domestic backlash concerning the extradition of Hasina. To date, Bangladesh has not officially responded to the Brics invitation.

Ahead of former Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina 's media address, the Indian government sought to distance itself from the event saying that India doesn't endorse the views that may be expressed at the event. However, Dhaka, which had raised the issue with Indian high commissioner Dinesh Trivedi on Monday, remains unconvinced as diplomatic sources said allowing Hasina to make a political speech might rock an already unsteady relationship.Hasina, who has announced she plans to return to Bangladesh in December despite the death sentence awarded to her, is scheduled to virtually address a media event at the foreign correspondents' club on Wednesday evening. This would be Hasina's first media address since she fled to India after being deposed on August 5, 2024.The MEA said that the interaction was being organized by a private media entity. “The government has no involvement whatsoever in it. Neither does it endorse any views that may be expressed at the forum,” said spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal. The ministry recently told a Parliamentary committee that while providing refuge to Hasina, India had strictly adhered to the principle that no political activity is directed against any other country from Indian soil.The Indian government also for the first time confirmed that Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman had been invited by India for the BRICS summit that it will host in September. While PM Narendra Modi had earlier invited Rahman to India for a bilateral visit, the government said that the invitation on this occasion is for a BRICS outreach session and in Rahman's capacity as the current chair of BIMSTEC.While Bangladesh aspires for BRICS membership and has already received support from Russia and China for its candidature, Rahman will likely be wary of any domestic fallout of travelling to India amid the unresolved Hasina extradition issue. Jamaat-e-Islami's ascendancy as the primary opposition party may also restrict Rahman from soft-pedalling the Hasina issue. Dhaka has not yet formally accepted or declined the invitation that was extended by Modi to Rahman for BRICS.“You would be aware that a formal invitation for a bilateral visit to India was extended to the Bangladesh PM upon his assumption of office in Feb 2026. As far as the BRICS Summit is concerned, India has separately extended an invitation to Bangladesh PM in his capacity as the current Chair of BIMSTEC to attend the outreach session of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi,” said the spokesperson.“The invitation has been extended as per the standard practice being followed in BRICS for the outreach sessions. Other heads of regional groups have also been invited in a similar manner,” he added.
Article Summary: India has firmly denied any role in Sheikh Hasina's forthcoming media address. Dhaka expresses skepticism, worried that the address may jeopardize diplomatic ties. Meanwhile, Bangladesh's Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has received an invitation to the Brics summit from India.

Article Title: Govt dismisses reports of fuel quality issues, says checks on
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Dismissing reports of fuel quality issues at outlets, govt Tuesday said additional checks have been introduced by oil marketing companies (OMCs) to detect fuel contamination and adulteration.In a post on X, the petroleum ministry said OMCs were regularly monitoring fuel quality, water ingress and contamination, and that only two cases of chloride contamination had been detected so far."In addition to the advanced and elaborate testing protocols already in place, further checks have been instituted, including water ingress testing 8-12 times a day at over 87,000 outlets. Over 2,000 samples have also been tested for chloride/sulphide. Only two cases of chloride contamination have been found in the entire country till now, and sales from those pumps were suspended immediately," ministry said.It added that oil companies had been instructed to take proactive steps to detect any possible contamination across the fuel supply chain, and strict action would be taken if contamination or adulteration was found at any retail outlet.Through a series of infographics on X, ministry said there was "zero compromise" on quality benchmarks and that 302 tankers carrying 10,500 kilolitres of ethanol were rejected between July 2024 and June 2026 for failing quality standards.It added that ethanol used for blending must comply with BIS IS 15464, have a minimum purity of 99.6% and be accompanied by a certified quality report. The ministry said ethanol is stored in dedicated facilities to prevent contamination, its quality is monitored regularly to ensure consistency and every tanker is sampled from both the top and bottom before being accepted.Separately, govt has so far approved Rs 4,687 crore as interest subsidy for eligible ethanol projects under its various support schemes, minister of state for petroleum Suresh Gopi told Parliament Monday. Under the schemes, govt bears an interest subvention of 6% or 50% of the interest rate charged by lenders, whichever is lower, for five years on loans taken to set up new distilleries or expand existing ethanol production capacity.
Article Summary: Govt: OMCs regularly monitoring fuel quality, water ingress and contamination. Only two cases of chloride contamination had been detected so far. 302 tankers carrying 10,500 kilolitres of ethanol were rejected between July 2024 and June 2026.

Article Title: 'Contamination' in fuel, says SIAM, later retracts
Article Text:
SIAM says corrosion of vehicle parts due to high chloride presence in fuel

NEW DELHI: Auto industry body SIAM flagged concerns over "high chloride" presence and moisture content in fuel resulting in a "huge increase" in issues related to vehicle parts and replacements, including fuel pumps, fuel injectors and EGR valve. It demanded stringent checks, arguing that contamination raises a wrong impression about E20 fuel in customers' minds, report Dipak Dash & Aabhas Sharma.Late evening, SIAM said it has since "withdrawn" the letter sent to petroleum ministry on July 28 that had raised these concerns, which were based on investigations of failure of vehicle parts.Some numbers quoted in the communication need authentication through collection of elaborate data from various regions across the country followed by a comprehensive consultation with our member OEMs. MoPNG has also instituted 3ppm guidelines for chloride/sulphur as a precautionary measure for all ethanol being blended into petrol supply chain, SIAM clarified late Tuesday.“All of these steps fully meet the needs of the automobile industry. Further, we understand from OMCs that checks have been instituted, including water ingress testing about 8-12 times a day in over 87,000 outlets,” it added. In the letter sent to ministry, SIAM had said investigations of failure of vehicle parts revealed that these were due to “corrosion or wear caused by high chloride presence traced to the fuel used”.It had urged the govt to “include chloride parameter” in E20 fuel specifications and its control by oil marketing companies and retail fuel outlets.SIAM said chloride was highly detrimental to engine parts as its presence or accumulation in the fuel system can lead to corrosion, which can further result in “permanent damage” to engine parts immediately or over time. “Hence, it is imperative to include the chloride limits in fuel specifications and implement quality control to avoid chloride related failures in the customer vehicles,” the letter had noted.
Article Summary: Auto industry body SIAM flagged concerns over "high chloride" presence and moisture content in fuel. It demanded stringent checks, arguing that contamination raises a wrong impression about E20 fuel in customers' minds. SIAM said it has since "withdrawn" the letter sent to petroleum ministry on July 28 that had raised these concerns.

NEW DELHI: Paving the way for expediting a new railway line to boost connectivity to the border area near the India-China-Bhutan tri-junction, West Bengal govt has given its go ahead for fast-tracking acquisition of around 380 hectares of land. With this, work on the 20-km Chalsa-Naxak new line project that was originally sanctioned in 2011-12 is likely to get speeded up.TOI has learnt that the new section, a vital component of the New Jalpaiguri-Siliguri-New Bongaigaon gauge conversion project was placed in abeyance in Sept 2019 due to non-cooperation from the earlier Trinamool govt in the state. Official records show that railways "de-freezed" (revived) the project in Jan along with five others after a six year hiatus but again failed to make any progress with the lack of support from the state govt's side.They added that soon after BJP formed govt all projects pending for years are being expedited. "Soon after Suvendu Adhikari took charge, railway minister Ashwini Vashnaw visited the state where all pending projects were reviewed and state govt has given the go ahead, including for this strategically important project," Siliguri MP Raju Bista told TOI.Earlier in the day, in a social media post, Bista said, "Happy to share that the ministry of railways has sanctioned around Rs 272 crore for a new 17-km line to Jaldhaka.The route originates from Khunia More near Chalsa, and passes through Jalpaiguri and Kalimpong forest divisions." He added that the rail link will improve connectivity to the India-China-Bhuta trijunction and boost tourism in the Jhaldhaka-Bindu-Todey Tangta area.Bista said, "The railways and Bengal forest department will carry out a joint survey after the monsoon for the proposed new line." It will connect Jaldhaka region, on the border of the river originating from a place close to Doklam tri-junction of India, Bhutan, China.

Article Title: Stalker uses husband's name to lure teacher to school gate, stabs her 20 times in Faridabad
Article Text:
Footage shows accused lunge at Sandhya the moment she reaches the classroom entrance, and pull her to the corridor

GURGAON: A stalker who allegedly pursued a 26-year-old teacher for nearly two years walked into a private school in Faridabad on Monday morning, tricked her into coming to the main gate by using her husband’s name, and then stabbed her more than 20 times in a vicious attack in front of staff and students until the blade bent.Captured on CCTV cameras, the attack unfolded in seconds and left the young English teacher dead before she could be taken to hospital.The accused, Amit (21), a resident of Kot village in Faridabad, was arrested within a couple of hours. Police said he had been stalking Sandhya, who taught at Saraswati Senior Secondary School in Sikrona, and attacked her after she allegedly severed all contact with him and warned him she would approach police if he continued to harass her.Amit entered the school around 9.30am, his face partially covered with a scarf, and asked staff to inform Sandhya that “Vicky” had come to meet her, referring to her husband. Believing her husband was waiting outside, she walked towards the entrance.Footage shows him lunge at Sandhya the moment she reaches the classroom entrance, and pull her to the corridor. Amit punches her as she cries out for help, pulls out a knife in a flash and goes on a stabbing fit, puncturing her neck, abdomen and upper body several times as she slumps to the ground.School principal Tejpal is seen rushing into the corridor to rescue Sandhya after hearing her screams but is forced to step back as the attacker threatens him with the knife.“There were students inside the school and Sandhya was taking classes. He used her husband’s name to call her outside. No sooner did he reach the gate, he attacked her. He stabbed her over 20 times. When I tried to stop him, he threatened to attack me too. We rushed her to Al-Falah Medical College, where she was declared dead on arrival,” the principal told TOI.Police sources said Amit had allegedly bought the knife around two months ago and is suspected to have been planning the murder since then. While the exact number of stab wounds will be confirmed after the autopsy, CCTV footage showed him stabbing Sandhya about 20 times in just 13 seconds. Amit had come to the school on a motorcycle.Sandhya, who had a love marriage with Vikas, is survived by their two children — a five-year-old son and a three-year-old daughter. The attack triggered panic on the campus. Teachers quickly moved frightened children back into classrooms while parents began arriving after news spread. Police cordoned off the school as forensic teams collected evidence.Based on a complaint by Sandhya’s husband, a case was registered under Section 103(1) (murder) of BNS at Sector 58 police station.Police spokesperson Yashpal Yadav said the anti-vehicle theft squad and a team from Sikrona police station tracked down Amit within two hours.“During questioning, the accused said he knew Sandhya from the school in his village where she earlier taught. She later stopped speaking to him and warned of legal action if he continued following her,” Yadav added.Police said the accused will be produced before a local court and his custody sought for further interrogation. CCTV footage and other evidence are being examined as part of the probe, they added.
Article Summary: A stalker walked into a private school in Faridabad on Monday morning, tricked her into coming to the main gate by using her husband’s name. He then stabbed her more than 20 times in a vicious attack in front of staff and students until the blade bent. The accused, Amit (21), a resident of Kot village infaridabad, was arrested within a couple of hours.

Article Title: In MP village, kids risk lives every day, hop over dam pillars to reach school
Article Text:
Children in Vidisha district risk daily commutes across a river

Poll Vote & Share your view Is the current education system in rural areas, like Kakraua, sufficient to support students? Yes, it meets their needs. No, it needs significant improvement. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





BHOPAL: Children from Kakraua village in MP's Vidisha district are forced to risk their lives every day by negotiating a precarious line of concrete pillars across a check dam on the Betwa river to reach their school - a route they take to avoid a much longer commute.A video of the children hopping perilously across the wide gaps in the check dam has gone viral on social media, raising fresh concerns about local infrastructure and student safety.Kakraua has a school only up to eighth grade.The nearest facility offering education up to 10th grade lies 13km away by road. By crossing the check dam, the distance shrinks to roughly 1.5km, prompting nine students - five of them girls in the ninth grade - to use the risky shortcut daily.The village is part of the constituency of former CM Shivraj Singh Chouhan, who is now the Union minister for agriculture.The dam-crossing involves walking across a series of exposed pillars that stand about three to four feet apart.Students hop about 10 pillars each trip. Villagers say the gap between pillars makes the route hazardous, especially during the monsoon when surfaces become slippery and the river's current increases."We have to work in the fields, so we can't drop our children off at school and back," said a parent."They find it easier to cross the dam nearby... We only have two options: we either stop sending our children to school or continue sending them this way even though it's dangerous."The consequences of skipping the unsafe route are already visible in the community.A student failed her final exams earlier this year after missing school because she could not cross the pillars due to her short height; she is repeating ninth grade this year.Parents fear that continued reliance on the shortcut could lead to further academic setbacks or, worse, an accident.District education officer N K Ahirwar acknowledged the problem. "I visited the spot and informed the collector about this," Ahirwar said."I have written to higher authorities to find a solution soon." However, he did not provide a timeline for the construction of a safe passage for river crossing.Local residents are now pressing authorities for an urgent solution to ensure uninterrupted schooling without endangering children's lives.
Article Summary: Children in Vidisha district risk daily commutes across a river to reach their school. A video of the children hopping perilously across the wide gaps in the check dam has gone viral on social media. The nearest facility offering education up to 10th grade lies 13km away by road.

Article Title: 'Arrest Abhijeet Dipke immediately': Social media influencer files complaint against CJP founder
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Social media influencer Faizan Ansari on Tuesday said he has filed a written complaint with the Delhi Police against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke, alleging that men linked to the party attacked him in Maharashtra.Ansari claimed he has evidence to support his allegations and urged the police to arrest Dipke immediately."Today, I have filed a written complaint against Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of the CJP party, with the Delhi DCP, because I have proof that his men attacked me. I was attacked in Pune and in Aurangabad. There are already 2 cases filed on that, " Ansari told ANI.He also praised the Delhi government and police for detaining activist Sonam Wangchuk during the recent protests, claiming the move prevented the law and order situation in the national capital from worsening."I want the Delhi police to immediately arrest Dipke. Moreover, I salute the Delhi CM and the police for detaining Sonam Wangchuk at the right time, due to which the atmosphere in Delhi was saved from deteriorating. Dipke is doing everything for his own benefit, " Ansari added“Moreover, I salute the Delhi CM and the police for detaining Sonam Wangchuk at the right time, due to which the atmosphere in Delhi was saved from deteriorating.Dipke is doing everything for his own benefit,” Ansari alleged.Earlier on Monday, Dipke had rejected comparisons between the CJP-led protests over alleged recruitment and examination irregularities and anti-government movements in Bangladesh and Nepal, saying Indian protesters draw inspiration from Mahatma Gandhi's legacy of peaceful resistance.Dipke also spoke about the CJP's expansion plans, compensation for the families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide, and the state of education in India.Dipke also dismissed exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen's remarks comparing the CJP's protest in Delhi against exam irregularities with the 2024 movement that led to the ouster of former Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina's Awami League government.“Protests in Bangladesh, Nepal are being used to defame us; we are different," he asserted.“We showed during the recent protest in Delhi that we were following the Constitution and holding our demonstration peacefully. Parallels to the protests in Bangladesh and Nepal are being used to defame us.“We don’t need to look at Bangladesh or Nepal when we have Mahatma Gandhi from whom the world takes inspiration to protest,” Dipke said.People are drawing comparisons with the protests in Bangladesh and Nepal because the alleged police brutality reminded them of scenes from those countries, he said.“The students in India were not violent or aggressive. They got their heads, arms and legs broken but displayed restraint and sat peacefully at Jantar Mantar," Dipke said.
Article Summary: Social media influencer Faizan Ansari on Tuesday said he has filed a written complaint with the Delhi Police against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke. Article Title: Bankipur bypoll: Prashant Kishor adds a dash of yellow to Bihar palette of saffron & green
Article Text:
Jan Suraaj party workers celebrating Prashant Kishor's victory





PATNA: Bihar has been green. It has been saffron. Now Prashant Kishor brings yellow.Kishor, architect of poll victories for others, has finally written one for himself, winning his electoral debut in the Bankipur bypoll. It is a signal flare and perhaps a glimpse of a shifting political palette as Jan Suraaj broke through BJP’s saffron and RJD’s green duopoly.Born in Rohtas in 1977, Kishor studied in Buxar, completed his Class XII from Patna Science College, earned a BBA from Lucknow University and a master’s in healthcare management from ASCI, Hyderabad. He did a French language course in France before spending eight years in a UN-supported public health programme.National prominence came after helping design PM Modi’s successful 2014 LS campaign. His organisation, I-PAC, went on to work with multiple political parties. He advised former Bihar CM Nitish Kumar, former Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee and parties across Punjab, Andhra and Tamil Nadu, earning a reputation as one of the country’s most successful political consultants.After helping the Nitish-led Mahagathbandhan win in 2015, Kishor briefly joined JDU before returning to grassroots politics.A self-professed believer in Gandhi’s philosophy, he spent nearly two years on a padayatra across Bihar before launching Jan Suraaj Party on Oct 2, 2024. Its candidates drew a blank in the 2025 state polls, raising questions over whether his campaign skills could translate into votes.Barely eight months later, the answer arrived in Bankipur. Defeat would have dealt a crushing blow to both Kishor and Jan Suraaj. Instead, victory fuelled debate over whether Bihar has room for a third political force.“I did not contest to become an MLA or turn Bankipur into a metropolitan city like Bengaluru,” he said. “I wanted to send a message to BJP brass — generate employment, provide education and stop migration, or be prepared for similar results.”Married to Dr Jahnavi Das and father to a son, Kishor lives like a monk on campaign. He rarely watches TV news, hasn’t used a laptop in a decade, and relies only on his phone to stay connected with his grassroots network.
Article Summary: Prashant Kishor, architect of poll victories for others, has finally written one for himself, winning his electoral debut in the Bankipur bypoll. It is a signal flare and perhaps a glimpse of a shifting political palette as Jan Suraaj broke through BJP's saffron and RJD's green duopoly.

NEW DELHI: Govt is likely to allow a levy of 0.25% to 0.4% as merchant discount rate (MDR) or charges on UPI payments above Rs 2,000 made to businesses, while keeping payments made by one person to another outside the ambit.The Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, moved by FM Nirmala Sitharaman on Tuesday, has sought to remove the bar on banks and payment service providers to levy MDR on notified electronic payment modes. Govt officials said there is no decision on when the proposal will be implemented.Official estimates show that the Rs 2,000 floor will cover 5% of all UPI transactions, but those transactions account for 65% of the total transaction value, and is unlikely to impact daily purchases such as milk, vegetables and groceries or even payments for auto or taxi use. In July, there were 23.7 billion transactions, whose combined value was pegged at Rs 29.9 lakh crore."Even if implemented, 95% of the transactions will not face the merchant discount rate. Besides, not all businesses are going to pass on the fees, which will be a small amount," an official said.Industry persons said govt may likely impose a ceiling on the absolute amount that is charged. "Unlike credit cards, there is no funding cost involved so it makes sense to have a ceiling once the costs are covered," said an industry source.At present, credit and debit cards come with MDR, but most merchants do not pass it on to consumers. In the case of credit card MDR, where the fee is not regulated, it can be as high as 3% of the transaction value. For debit card transactions up to Rs 20 lakh, there is a cap of 0.4%, and for higher value it is 0.9%.
Article Summary: The Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, moved by FM Nirmala Sitharaman on Tuesday, has sought to remove the bar on banks and payment service providers to levy MDR on notified electronic payment modes. Govt officials said there is no decision on when the proposal will be implemented.

Article Title: 56% of vehicles not insured, SC says challan them
Article Text:
SC has raised alarm on the uninsured vehicles operating on road

NEW DELHI: If your vehicle is not insured, you may not be able to get fuel from petrol pumps in the near future. Supreme Court Tuesday suggested this as one of the measures to tackle the problem of uninsured vehicles plying on roads and also directed that cameras deployed on highways and roads be used to identify such vehicles and send challans to owners.Expressing shock that nearly 56% of vehicles plying on Indian roads remain uninsured (most of them two-wheelers), a bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Prashant Kumar Mishra said the purpose behind mandatory insurance under Section 146 of the Motor Vehicles Act gets defeated, resulting in victims of road accidents being forced into prolonged litigation to get compensation. In absolute terms, the stark figure of uninsured vehicles stands at 16.5 crore vehicles out of a total of 30.4 crore registered vehicles. As per govt data, 22% of road accidents involve uninsured vehicles.As per the MV Act, those who drive or allow an uninsured vehicle to be driven without valid motor third-party insurance are liable to be punished, including imprisonment, for violation of the law. In the case of a first offence, the punishment is imprisonment for up to three months, or a fine of Rs 2,000 or both; and for a subsequent offence, imprisonment for up to three months, or a fine of Rs 4,000 or both are provided."The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority, in consultation with the road transport ministry, to deliberate and evolve a pilot project whereby fuel for vehicles to be linked with valid insurance status. In the absence thereof, the vehicle concerned would be refused fuel at petrol pumps until such time valid insurance is obtained. The benefit therein is two-fold - first, it will assist in identification of uninsured or unregistered vehicles. Secondly, it will prompt the owners of these vehicles to ensure that they have valid insurance status. Such projects would ensure ground-level compliance with the statutory mandate of Section 146 of the MVA. This may be done through the use of cameras. The ministry of petroleum and natural gas, has in principle, no objection to the same," the bench said.The bench said that there should be strict implementation of law and directed that state traffic police should be given handheld devices or downloadable apps, linked with the data from Insurance Information Bureau and VAHAN portal to verify insurance status on the ground. "ANPR cameras deployed on highways and roads are equipped with a mechanism to catch and penalise road safety violations such as high speed, red light jumping, driving on the wrong side of the road, etc. Carrying this forward and as already deployed by the MoRTH in certain states, ANPR cameras are to be integrated with data from the Insurance Information Bureau and the VAHAN portal for issuance of automatic e-challans to uninsured vehicles," the bench said.The result of vehicles remaining uninsured is that accident victims and their families have no recourse to adequate compensation within a reasonable time period.In 2018, the apex court had directed mandatory buying of third-party insurance for three years for new cars and five years for two-wheelers at the time of buy/registration of new vehicles. Noting that a large number of vehicles remain uninsured, the bench increased the period by one year and directed that henceforth, a buyer has to buy third-party insurance for four years for new cars and six years for new two-wheelers.
Article Summary: Nearly 56% of vehicles plying on Indian roads remain uninsured (most of them two-wheelers) 16.5 crore vehicles out of a total of 30.4 crore registered vehicles. 22% of road accidents involve uninsured vehicles. Those who drive or allow uninsured vehicle to be driven without valid motor third-party insurance are liable to be punished.

Article Title: US Congressman warns FCRA Bill could affect India-US ties

A US lawmaker on Tuesday criticised the amendments proposed to India's foreign funding law, alleging that they could allow the government to take over churches and religious charities and warning that the issue could affect India-US ties.US Congressman Riley Moore said the proposed changes to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) amounted to "a clear attack against Christians" and urged India not to proceed with the legislation in its current form.In a post on X, the Republican Congressman from West Virginia said Christianity had a long history in India dating back to the arrival of St Thomas the Apostle on the Malabar Coast."But despite this long Christian history, India's Parliament is considering amending Foreign Contribution Regulation Amendment (FCRA) rules to permit government takeovers of churches and religious charities," Moore wrote."This is a clear attack against Christians. If this bill proceeds in this way, it would be a point of major concern in our bilateral relationship with India," he added.The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 proposes the creation of a Designated Authority that would take over the management of foreign contributions and assets created using such funds if an organisation's FCRA registration is cancelled, surrendered or lapses after not being renewed.The Bill specifies that where such assets include a place of worship, the Designated Authority must ensure that its religious character is preserved.It also proposes reducing the maximum punishment for violations of the Act from five years' imprisonment to one year.The FCRA regulates the receipt and utilisation of foreign contributions by NGOs, charitable trusts, educational institutions, religious bodies and other associations. According to the Ministry of Home Affairs, 13,520 organisations received foreign contributions worth Rs 55,741 crore between 2019 and 2022.Government data shows that as of July 15, 2026, there were 14,449 active FCRA registrations, while 22,498 had been cancelled and another 15,212 had expired.

Article Title: Indian cargo vessel sinks after attack in Yemeni waters; all 14 crew rescued

A projectile attack sank the Indian-flagged vessel off Yemen, but all 14 crew members, including 13 Indians, were safely rescued. (Representational image)

NEW DELHI: An Indian-flagged cargo vessel was struck by a projectile and sank off Yemen’s western coast on Tuesday. All 14 crew members aboard the vessel were rescued and brought to safety.Union minister for ports, shipping and waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, said the MSV Faize Noore Oliya was hit by a projectile in Yemeni waters, causing it to capsize and sink. The crew comprised 13 Indian nationals and one Yemeni sailor.The Yemeni Coast Guard rescued all 14 crew members and brought them safely to the port of Mokha, Sonowal added. No casualties were reported.Ministry of External Affairs said the vessel sank in the Red Sea off the Yemeni coast on August 4 and confirmed that all 13 Indian nationals had been rescued. The Indian Embassy in Riyadh was coordinating with Yemeni authorities to ensure the safety of the crew and provide necessary assistance.The government-affiliated National Resistance Forces said coast guard and naval units carried out a joint rescue operation after the vessel was attacked about 13 nautical miles (24 km) south of the Houthi-held port city of Hodeidah.The National Resistance Forces blamed Yemen’s Houthi rebels for the attack.The Houthis have not commented on the incident.Sonowal condemned what he called an “unprovoked attack” and said the safety of Indian seafarers remained the government’s “supreme priority”. He said the Director General of Maritime Administration had been instructed to coordinate with relevant agencies to ensure the security of Indian sailors in the region.The MEA also expressed concern over continued attacks on commercial shipping in the region, saying such targeting “must end”. It called for free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through international waterways in the region, in accordance with international law, to be restored at the earliest.
Article Summary: The MSV Faize Noore Oliya was hit by a projectile in Yemeni waters, causing it to capsize and sink. The Yemeni Coast Guard rescued all 14 crew members and brought them safely to the port of Mokha. No casualties were reported.

Article Title: Day after PK's poll win, PM Modi talks to Nabin, meets Nitish

Article Title: Sudden drop in altitude: Flyers injured as Air India's Phuket-Delhi flight encounters turbulence
Article Text:
Air India flight from Phuket to Delhi experienced turbulence-related event during cruise. (Photo: TOI)

NEW DELHI: Some passengers and crew members onboard Air India's Phuket-Delhi flight (AI 2379) suffered injuries when the aircraft encountered turbulence Tuesday morning, causing a sudden drop in altitude by 300 feet. An AI with medical support received the 134 passengers onboard the Airbus A320 on arrival just after 11 am. Over 10 passengers and two crew members are learnt to have been taken to the Medanta medical centre at the airport. Subsequently, 14 injured - 10 passengers and four crew members - were shifted to Medanta Hospital in Gurugram and India Spinal Injury Centre in Vasant Kunj.An AI spokesperson said the aircraft “experienced a brief in-flight turbulence-related event during cruise, resulting in a momentary change in altitude. The aircraft landed safely in Delhi and all passengers and crew have safely disembarked. There have been no serious injuries reported as of now. A small number of passengers and crew members with minor injuries requiring medical assessment have been taken to a medical facility at the airport for precautionary examination and care by Air India’s airport team and medical personnel.The A320 had taken off from Phuket at 8.27 am and landed in Delhi just after 11 am (all timings local).“The safety and well-being of our passengers and crew remain Air India’s highest priority. We are providing all necessary support to those affected and are cooperating fully with the relevant authorities as part of the investigation,” the spokesperson added.Aircraft frequently experience clear air turbulence (CAT), which International Civil Aviation Organisation defines as turbulence generated in clear air, in regions without clouds that is invisible to the pilot and by the US Federal Aviation Administration as sudden severe turbulence occurring in cloudless regions that causes violent buffeting of aircraft. Due to this possibility, it is advisable to have seatbelt loosely on during flight.
Article Summary: Some passengers and crew members onboard Air India's Phuket-Delhi flight suffered injuries. Aircraft encountered turbulence Tuesday morning, causing a sudden drop in altitude by 300 feet. Over 10 passengers and two crew members are learnt to have been taken to the Medanta medical centre at the airport. 14 injured were shifted to Medanta Hospital in Gurugram and India Spinal Injury Centre.

Article Title: '100% pure'? Stop misleading products' sale, FSSAI tells Dabur
Article Text:
FSSAI bars Dabur's 100 guarantee claims

NEW DELHI: If a food label says "100% pure", "100% natural" or "100% purity guaranteed", consumers may still need to read it with caution. In one of its strongest actions against misleading food labels, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has ordered Dabur India to stop selling a range of products carrying such claims, saying they violated food labelling regulations and could mislead buyers.The order covers products that include organic honey, apple cider vinegar, virgin coconut oil, sesame oil, cow ghee, coconut water and coconut milk, marketed with claims such as "100% juice", "100% purity" and "100% original".According to FSSAI, the company had made unauthorised organic claims, creating an impression of regulatory endorsement.The regulator also found that some claims on the labels were not permitted under Food Safety and Standards (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018.FSSAI has directed the company to immediately stop the sale of the identified products, recall products already in the market within 15 days and submit a compliance report.In a statement, Dabur said it believes the declarations on its product labels comply with the prevailing legal and regulatory framework and are consistent with long-standing industry practices. It said it stands by the purity and quality of its products and has never made misleading claims.Dabur said that it had begun removing the "100%" claims from product labels, advertisements and its website, in keeping with FSSAI's observations, adding that many products have already been updated while others are in the process of transition.It said that it is responding to the regulator, and will continue to engage constructively to resolve the matter.
Article Summary: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India orders Dabur India to stop selling a range of products carrying such claims. The order covers products that include organic honey, apple cider vinegar, virgin coconut oil, sesame oil, cow ghee, coconut water and coconut milk. The company had made unauthorised organic claims, creating an impression of regulatory endorsement.

Article Title: Rajya Sabha clears birth, death regn bill without any discussion

NEW DELHI: Rajya Sabha Tuesday passed Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill amid din, with MoS for home Nityanand Rai saying the legislation intends to ensure every child born is duly registered and also all deaths are registered "so that ghosts don't keep casting votes for parties that believe in appeasement".The bill was passed without any discussion and voice vote as an unrelenting opposition continued to disrupt proceedings over NEET-UG paper leak and Ram temple donation theft issues and demanding home minister Amit Shah's presence in the House.Responding to the discussion on the bill, Rai, in apparent reference to illegal immigrants, said, "The country now wants to get rid of ghosts. There are govts in some states that look for an opportunity and welcome those (who were not born in India) and register their births who are not eligible to be registered here. RS witnessed an uproar as governing party and opposition had an angry exchange of words over the donation theft issue.When LoP Malikarjun Kharge asked why govt agencies like ED, CBI and I-T were not probing the theft 'by members of Ram Janmbhoomi Teerth Kshetra', parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju alleged that Congress and SP had always "abused Lord Ram" and "opposed Ram Temple construction."

Article Title: Udhayanidhi: Udhayanidhi Stalin arrest drama: 'No double meaning in my speech; TN CM using diversion tactic,' says DMK leader - top developments

Arrested over alleged remarks linked to Trisha

NEW DELHI: DMK leader and leader of opposition in the Tamil Nadu Assembly Udhayanidhi Stalin was arrested on Tuesday over his alleged "double-meaning" remark linked to actor Trisha.While the Madras high court directed that he would be released on station bail after questioning, the day witnessed dramatic political developments, protests by DMK workers and a war of words between the ruling TVK government and the opposition.Addressing supporters after being released from Sengipatti Police Station, Udhayanidhi dismissed the case against him as politically motivated and accused the ruling TVK of using "diversion tactics and fake news".He maintained that his speech at the Thanjavur farmers' protest contained no double meaning and was intended only to demand Cauvery water for farmers."I don't have any intention to malign anyone. My parents did not nurture me that way. I have a family and a sister," he said. Thanking DMK cadres, senior leaders and the party's legal wing for standing by him, Udhayanidhi added that "foisting false cases will not stop me" and said he would continue raising farmers' issues.He also expressed disappointment that some political leaders criticised him without watching his full speech.Udhayanidhi Stalin walked out of the Sengipatti Police Station in Thanjavur after being questioned in connection with a case over his alleged remarks during a public meeting.As he emerged from the police station, the DMK leader was greeted by a large gathering of party cadres, who raised slogans in his support.Udhayanidhi acknowledged the crowd, waving and greeting supporters before leaving the premises.He had been detained earlier in the day and brought from Chennai for questioning.Also read| After arrest and 90-minute grilling, Udhayanidhi Stalin released by Thanjavur police The Madras high court had directed the police to release him after completing the inquiry and asked him to cooperate with the investigation whenever required.Questioning of Udhayanidhi Stalin began at the Sengipatti police station in Thanjavur district. After stepping out of the police vehicle that brought him from Chennai, the DMK leader waved at the large gathering of supporters outside before entering the police station for the inquiry.DMK cadres continued to assemble outside the premises, raising slogans in his support.After a brief delay, Udhayanidhi Stalin stepped out of the police van that brought him from Chennai and entered the Sengipatti police station in Thanjavur district for questioning.Meanwhile, DMK cadres have also started gathering in large numbers outside the police station, raising slogans in support of the leader of opposition as the inquiry gets underway.In the latest development, police changed the venue for Udhayanidhi Stalin's questioning, rerouting his convoy to Sengipatti between Thanjavur and Tiruchirappalli instead of the Thanjavur West police station, where he was initially expected to be questioned.Former DMK ministers K N Nehru, E V Velu and M R K Panneerselvam reached the Sengipatti police station and accompanied Udhayanidhi during the inquiry.Meanwhile, a large number of DMK cadres gathered near the Thanjavur West police station after reports initially suggested that he would be questioned there.Earlier in the day, the Madras high court directed the Tamil Nadu Police to release Udhayanidhi after completing the inquiry and asked him to cooperate with the investigation whenever required.During the hearing, advocate general Vijay Narayan informed the court that the police did not intend to seek Udhayanidhi's judicial remand."He has already been arrested but will be let off after questioning. We do not intend to remand Udhayanidhi Stalin. He will be released on station bail after inquiry," the advocate general told the court, according to news agency ANI.Udhayanidhi was taken into custody by the Thanjavur Police from his residence in Chennai's Neelankarai on Tuesday morning in connection with an FIR registered over his speech at a Cauvery protest in Thanjavur on Monday.He has been booked under multiple provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act and the Information Technology Act.Also read| Smiles, waves and slogans: How Udhayanidhi’s arrest turned into a political spectacle Charges include allegedly using obscene words, insulting the modesty of a woman, promoting enmity, provoking riots and criminal intimidation.The controversy erupted after sections of the crowd chanted actor Trisha's name during his speech, following which he allegedly made a double-entendre remark.The women's wing of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) lodged a complaint, alleging that the remarks insulted the actor and women in general.Before being taken away by the police, Udhayanidhi maintained that he had not targeted anyone and said the matter would be decided by the courts."Did I mention anyone's name except the CM's? Then why do you think this is happening? Let the court decide," he told reporters.Later, he alleged that edited clips of his speech had been circulated to create a "fake narrative.""They have propagated fake news by using 'Cut, Copy, Paste' to claim I said something I never said. I am not the kind of person to be intimidated by all this. I will face it legally," he said, as quoted by ANI.The DMK has maintained that his remarks were misrepresented and were directed at the government's functioning rather than any individual.DMK president M K Stalin strongly criticised the TVK government over the arrest, accusing it of acting with "arrogance" and trying to stop Udhayanidhi from attending the Assembly budget session.Also read| 'Reel creator instead of CM': Stalin attacks Vijay over Udhayanidhi's arrest He alleged that police had "arrogantly" taken Udhayanidhi into custody from Chennai and transported him to Thanjavur under non-bailable charges. Stalin also claimed that the government's stand changed in court after public outrage, with its lawyers stating there was no intention to seek judicial custody.Calling the high court's order a setback for the government, Stalin demanded the immediate release of all DMK workers detained during protests across the state.AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami (EPS), criticised both Udhayanidhi Stalin's alleged remarks and the Vijay government's decision to arrest him ahead of the Assembly's budget session.In a post on X, EPS said Udhayanidhi's "degrading remarks about women" were "strongly condemnable" and claimed he had repeatedly said the DMK leader "needs a muzzle."However, he also questioned the timing of the arrest, alleging it appeared politically motivated and aimed at paralysing the Assembly by preventing the leader of the opposition from attending the session.EPS urged the government to withdraw the arrest action immediately.The arrest triggered protests by DMK cadres across Tamil Nadu, with workers staging demonstrations and road blockades condemning the police action.At the party headquarters, M K Stalin chaired a meeting to discuss the next course of action ahead of the Assembly session beginning on August 5.Senior leaders, including P K Sekar Babu, K N Nehru and Ma Subramanian, rallied behind Udhayanidhi, while the party moved the Madras High Court seeking anticipatory bail before his arrest.While the DMK defended Udhayanidhi, the ruling TVK intensified its attack.TVK spokesperson Americai Narayanan accused the DMK leader of insulting women during a protest meant to highlight farmers' issues, claiming that people had begun referring to him as "vulgar nidhi".Congress MP Jothimani also criticised Udhayanidhi, saying women should not be dragged into political battles and describing the remarks as "objectionable."The TVK has filed complaints with both the Thanjavur Police and the National Commission for Women, seeking action and an unconditional public apology from Udhayanidhi.Tamil Nadu electricity minister R Nirmal Kumar questioned Udhayanidhi's suitability for public office following the controversy.
Article Summary: DMK leader and leader of opposition in the Tamil Nadu Assembly Udhayanidhi Stalin was arrested on Tuesday over his alleged "double-meaning" remark linked to actor Trisha. The Madras high court directed the police to release him after completing the inquiry and asked him to cooperate with the investigation whenever required.

Article Title: Computer-based NEET? Govt tells SC decision after Nilekani report
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Centre Tuesday told Supreme Court that while the proposal to shift NEET from pen-and-paper mode to computer-based mode is under consideration, the final decision will be taken only after getting the report of the Nandan Nilekani-led high-powered task force set up to overhaul India's public examination systems.In an affidavit, govt briefed SC on measures taken to make the exam foolproof, including stringent penal provisions against use of unfair means and setting up of task force. It was responding to a plea by All India Medical Association seeking a more secure NEET following this year's paper leak.Govt said: "Migration from pen-and-paper mode to a computer-based mode, whether in single-stage or two-stage exam on the pattern of JEE, is presently under consideration by all stakeholders." The final approach, it added, would be adopted after considering the task force's recommendations.It said NTA has migrated seven of its eight major exams to computer-based testing. NEET (UG) remains its only major pen-and-paper exam.
Article Summary: Proposal to shift NEET from pen-and-paper mode to computer-based mode is under consideration. Final decision will be taken only after getting the report of the Nandan Nilekani-led high-powered task force set up to overhaul India's public examination systems.

Article Title: 'Will do whatever is necessary for national interest': India after Pakistan deploys 250 Chinese Howitzers
Article Text:
File photo: Chinese self-propelled artillery guns

Pakistan deploys Chinese SH-15 howitzers

India also modernising artillery

NEW DELHI: India on Tuesday said it would do "whatever is necessary" to safeguard its national interests after reports emerged that Pakistan had deployed a large number of Chinese-made SH-15 self-propelled artillery guns along the border facing India.Responding to a question during the ministry of external affairs' weekly media briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India's position remained unchanged on cross-border terrorism and asserted that the country would remain prepared to defend itself."During Operation Sindoor, we saw how a befitting reply was given (to Pakistan). From our side, our stance is that cross-border terrorism must stop, and we will do whatever is necessary in our national interest, for which we always remain vigilantly deployed," Jaiswal said.The remarks came a day after reports said Pakistan had deployed around 250 Chinese-origin SH-15 wheeled self-propelled howitzers in formations facing India as part of its artillery modernisation programme.In the briefing, Jaiswal also strongly criticised the recently held elections in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoK), describing them as a "complete farce" and accusing Pakistan of using force to suppress public dissent."This so-called local election in PoK is a complete farce. The real happening is that of public protests and wanton killings by Pakistani forces. Such hollow exercises cannot hide reality," Jaiswal said.He said that at least 90 civilians had been killed since June during the crackdown in PoK."Since June this year, at least 90 civilians have lost their lives in the continuing crackdown. The Pakistani Establishment has answered public discontent with bullets, blackouts, intimidation and repression, and now seeks to manufacture legitimacy through a hollow electoral exercise," he said, urging the international community to hold Islamabad accountable.Jaiswal also responded to a media inquiry about a viral video in which members of the Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba claimed that 30 to 40 of their commanders had been killed, alleging that Indian agencies were responsible for the killings.He said, "We continue to call upon all countries to take strong action against cross-border terrorism and those who promote it. We also call upon Pakistan to take decisive action against cross-border terrorism and dismantle the terrorist infrastructure operating from its soil."Pakistan ordered 236 SH-15 155mm/52-calibre wheeled self-propelled artillery guns from Chinese state-owned defence firm Norinco in 2019, with deliveries beginning in 2022 and a second batch arriving in 2023.Pakistan has also acquired a transfer of technology agreement to manufacture the artillery system at Heavy Industries Taxila.The SH-15, known as the PCL-181 in China, has reportedly been deployed mainly in Pakistan's Gujranwala, Sialkot and Jalalpur Jattan sectors opposite India, particularly around the Shakargarh Bulge.The guns were also used during Operation Sindoor.The 155mm artillery system is capable of firing multiple types of ammunition and has a range of more than 50 kilometres when using rocket-assisted projectiles.Retired Lieutenant General PR Shankar, former Director General of Artillery, told TOI that the acquisition strengthens Pakistan's conventional firepower and complements its Army Rocket Force, enhancing its long-range strike capabilities.The deployment comes as India continues to modernise its own artillery under the Field Artillery Rationalisation Plan.The Indian Army has inducted 155mm artillery systems such as the M777 ultra-light howitzer, the K-9 Vajra self-propelled gun and the indigenous Dhanush gun. It has also placed orders for 307 Advanced Towed Artillery Gun Systems (ATAGS), developed domestically.India is also working on a wheeled Mounted Gun System (MGS), based on the ATAGS platform, which is currently in the advanced stages of development and has undergone initial firing trials.
Article Summary: India says it will do "whatever is necessary" to safeguard its national interests. India's position remains unchanged on cross-border terrorism, says MEA spokesperson. Pakistan has deployed 250 Chinese-origin SH-15 wheeled self- propelled howitzers in formations facing India.

Article Title: Govt proposes mandatory Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication systems from Oct 2028 to cut road crashes
Article Text:
All new cars, passenger and goods vehicles would need to have Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication system. (PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From Oct 2028, all new two- and three-wheelers, cars, passenger and goods vehicles (including buses and trucks) would need to have Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication system, as per a draft notification of the road transport ministry. The V2V technology is being rolled out to curb collisions and accidents.The recently published draft notification by road transport ministry proposes phased implementation of the V2V communication system and to start with all vehicles in categories L (two- and three-wheelers), M (passenger vehicles) and N (goods vehicles) manufactured from Oct 2027 would be required to comply with the newly-notified automotive standard, AIS-230, wherever they are equipped with V2V communication systems.The technology enables real-time exchange of speed, direction, position, and braking data between vehicles to prevent collisions at blind curves, intersections, or from drivers coming the wrong way without needing a cellular network. Each vehicle needs to be fitted with a device that will automatically detect approaching vehicles for preventing any crash.Unlike conventional vehicle-safety systems, which primarily depend on onboard sensors and driver reaction, V2V communication can provide information beyond the direct line of sight.“It is therefore expected to complement Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and support proactive accident prevention, connected mobility and future intelligent transport applications,” the ministry said.In this case, every vehicle fitted with the V2V communication system will continuously send out their locations, speed and direction as tiny radio signals. They will also relay information on sudden braking by a vehicle ahead, forward collision risks, unsafe lane changes, wrong-way driving and the approach of emergency vehicles.The receiving vehicle’s system compares this information with its own location, speed and direction to predict a possible collision and alerts the driver for action.At a later stage, govt will also roll out the Vehicle to Infrastructure (V2I) communication system. In this case, sensors are installed with infrastructure, such as signal and power poles, edges of bridges and flyovers, and barricaded areas to alert vehicles.
Article Summary: All new cars, passenger and goods vehicles would need to have Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication system. The V2V technology is being rolled out to curb collisions and accidents. Each vehicle needs to be fitted with a device that will automatically detect approaching vehicles for preventing any crash.

Article Title: Cyber crime reports down from 1.2L in 2024 to 16,377 now: Government
Article Text:
Supreme Court urged prompt action against cyber fraudsters, while noting a reduction in incidents. Authorities were directed to expedite decisions on a 'kill switch' for phones. Monies transferred to mule accounts will be placed on hold by banks. Victims will receive recovered amounts expeditiously after investigations conclude. New directives aim to enhance cyber crime grievance redressal mechanisms.

NEW DELHI: Despite 75% reduction in cyber-crime and digital arrest incidents, Supreme Court continued to push authorities for prompt action against cyber fraudsters by issuing a slew of directives Tuesday, including an expeditious decision on a 'kill switch' in phones to prevent these crimes and placing on hold monies transferred to mule accounts.Attorney general R Venkataramani told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that number of complaints on national cyber crime portal had gone down from 1,23,672 in 2024 to 16,377 in 2026 (as of June 30). Besides, an Rs 18 crore has been restored to around 36,000 cyber fraud victims, he said in a status report.While appreciating the progress made in the matter, which the court is monitoring after taking suo motu cognisance on Oct 16 last year, bench directed Reserve Bank of India to formally "adopt and circulate formal standard operating procedure within four weeks detailing the action to be taken by banks for placing temporary hold on amounts and accounts in mule accounts linked to cyber fraud".Accepting a suggestion of amicus curiae N S Nappinai, SC also directed states, UTs and law enforcing agencies to take steps for expeditious adoption and operationalisation of grievance redressal and money restoration modules of home ministry, which should be given adequate publicity to enable victims to take required remedial measures.CJI-led bench directed "all adjudicatory authorities, including RBI ombudsman, consumer fora, courts and law enforcing authorities - to ensure that amounts recovered from fraudsters are disbursed to victims of digital arrest expeditiously".It asked RBI to file a status report on this aspect by Sept 16, the next date of hearing.Even as CBI continues investigations into digital scams, the court asked agency to examine AG's suggestion for lowering the present threshold of Rs 10 crore for taking up investigations into cases where the same gang of scamsters are involved."The proposal concerning a time-based 'Kill switch' for audio and video calls may be examined by ministry of information and technology, Department of Telecom and Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) in consultation with telecom intermediaries and a brief note on technical feasibility, efficacy, safeguards and alternatives be placed on record," the bench said.It asked Inter-Departmental Committee (IDC), which coordinates with various departments for steps to prevent digital arrest and cyber crime offences, to issue necessary directives on setting up of cyber crime grievance redressal mechanism and restoration of defrauded amounts to victims.
Article Summary: Supreme Court issues slew of directives against cyber fraudsters. Authorities directed to expedite decisions on a 'kill switch' for phones. Monies transferred to mule accounts will be placed on hold by banks. Victims will receive recovered amounts expeditiously after investigations conclude.

Article Title: WA tests optional age verification pilot, says user privacy will be protected
Article Text:
To comply with the upcoming Digital Personal Data Protection Act, WhatsApp is piloting new privacy-focused age verification methods for Indian users. This initiative is completely voluntary, allowing users to choose their participation. With the new law's emphasis on stricter regulations for children's personal data, WhatsApp is taking care to safeguard user privacy during this important verification process.

NEW DELHI: In a bid to comply with the upcoming Digital Personal Data Protection Act, WhatsApp has begun testing optional age verification methods for users in India. The Meta-owned messaging service said the pilot is designed to verify a user's age in a privacy-protective manner and that participation in the test is voluntary."To comply with upcoming laws in India like Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDP), we are testing privacy-protective ways for people to confirm their age. This doesn't change how WhatsApp works or your experience. We understand that information about someone's age is private and it won't be shared with other WhatsApp users," a WhatsApp spokesperson said.The company clarified that users do not have to confirm their age to continue using WhatsApp during the test.The development comes as digital platforms prepare for the implementation of the DPDP framework, which introduces stricter obligations for companies handling children's personal data. Under the law, a child is defined as anyone below the age of 18, and companies processing children's personal data are required to obtain verifiable parental consent and put in place safeguards to protect young users.WhatsApp has not disclosed how long the pilot will run or the specific methods being evaluated for age verification. The company said the exercise is aimed at ensuring compliance while preserving user privacy.
Article Summary: To comply with the upcoming Digital Personal Data Protection Act, WhatsApp is piloting new privacy-focused age verification methods for Indian users. The company said the exercise is aimed at ensuring compliance while preserving user privacy.

Article Title: Government to grill Meta brass on child abuse, AI content
Article Text:
In an important meeting scheduled for this week, government officials will confront Meta executives regarding pressing issues. The discussions will center around the presence of child sexual abuse material, the rise of AI-created content, and the measures in place for takedowns involving notable personalities. Compliance with local laws and the efficiency of Meta's content moderation efforts, particularly in monitoring synthetic content, are also poised to be key topics of concern.

Want to know how Meta is tackling CSAM: Govt

NEW DELHI: Govt will press Meta on child sexual abuse material, AI-generated content and safeguards around takedown of posts by prominent personalities, including PM Modi, when the company's senior executives meet officials here this week, reports Aabhas Sharma.MeitY secretary S Krishnan said Meta executives, including Joel Kaplan, head of Meta's public policy, are expected to meet govt officials on Wednesday and Thursday, with discussions set to cover compliance with Indian laws, content moderation and challenges posed by AI content.MeitY secretary S Krishnan said Tuesday, “We want to ensure that compliance happens. There are a range of issues.”He said govt wants to know what measures Meta has taken to tackle CSAM on its platforms and how effectively it is monitoring synthetically generated content. “CSAM issue has been raised, and we want to know what measures have been taken to address it. We also want to understand to what extent synthetically-generated content is being monitored,” he said.Krishnan also flagged concerns over the removal of content posted by verified accounts of prominent personalities, saying that such actions should be backed by stronger safeguards.
Article Summary: MeitY secretary S Krishnan said Meta executives, including Joel Kaplan, head of Meta's public policy, are expected to meet govt officials on Wednesday and Thursday. discussions set to cover compliance with Indian laws, content moderation and challenges posed by AI content.

Article Title: Census phase 2 likely to accept half-filled forms
Article Text:
In the first phase of the census — involving housing and houselisting operations — those opting for self-enumeration were not able to submit the form with blank fields

NEW DELHI: Census authorities are considering allowing persons self-enumerating for the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 to submit a partially filled form online.In the first phase of the census - involving housing and houselisting operations - those opting for self-enumeration were not able to submit the form with blank fields. If any field was left blank - either accidentally or intentionally due to lack of clarity - the user could not advance to the submission window.Sources said that it was felt during discussions among census teams that this feature forced many to opt out of self-enumeration and rely on the enumerator's visit to record their replies to the questionnaire.There is now a realisation that even a partially filled form, provided a minimum number of questions are answered, would help in easing the task of the enumerator. Besides, self-declared data tends to be more accurate and reliable."Internal deliberations focused on why the self-enumeration option should not be made flexible, given that the data is to be entered digitally either by the respondent or the enumerator.The census application anyway allows the enumerator to access the filled-up form and change any wrongly entered data. So why can't he access a partially filled-up form and fill in the few remaining fields during the house visit, saving time and effort?" an officer told TOI.The population enumeration exercise is set to be conducted nationwide in Feb 2027. However, the exercise, as per convention, is advanced for select states/UTs like Ladakh, J&K, HP and Uttarakhand that become wholly or partially snow-bound in Feb. These areas will witness population enumeration from Sept 1 to 30, preceded by a self-enumeration window of Aug 17-30.
Article Summary: In the first phase of the census, those opting for self-enumeration were not able to submit the form with blank fields. Article Title: Tie compensation to functional disability, says SC
Article Text:
The doctor certified her 90% disabled, but a bench held that she was suffering from 100% functional disability

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Holding that functional disability faced by a road accident victim should be the deciding factor for granting compensation and not doctor-certified medical disability, SC has granted compensation of Rs 83.3 lakh to a minor who met with an accident when she was just six months old and is now suffering from severe spinal cord and neurological injuries.Though the doctor certified her 90% disabled, a bench held that she was suffering from 100% functional disability and quantified the compensation on that basis."...In the given facts of a case, a lesser physical disability may result in a much higher functional disability and in an appropriate case, even amount to complete loss of earning capacity," the bench said, adding it would be reasonable to assume that functional incapacity resulting out of a particular bodily injury may be higher and greater than what may be medically perceived."The present case concerns a child who has suffered permanent disability at a tender age and whose future stands altered on account of the injuries sustained in the accident. In such circumstances, the court is required to adopt an approach which is realistic, humane and consistent with the settled principles governing award of compensation under the MV Act," the bench said while increasing the amount of compensation to over Rs 83 lakh."Cases involving child victims suffering permanent or near total disability constitute a distinct and special category within the law relating to motor accident compensation. A child, by reason of age, vulnerability and complete dependence upon others, stands on an altogether different footing from an adult claimant. The consequences of a catastrophic injury suffered during childhood are not confined merely to the immediate physical impairment caused by the accident.Such injuries alter the entire course of the child's existence and affect every subsequent stage of her life. The law, therefore, cannot evaluate claims involving injured children through the same lens that may ordinarily be applied in cases involving adults," it said.
Article Summary: A minor who met with an accident when she was just six months old is now suffering from severe spinal cord and neurological injuries. Though the doctor certified her 90% disabled, a bench held that she was suffering from 100% functional disability and quantified the compensation on that basis.

Article Title: Government: 20 died in heatstrokes across 4 states
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Twenty people have died due to heatstroke across four states while 4,853 cases of heatstroke were reported across country since March 1 this year, home ministry informed Lok Sabha Tuesday. Maharashtra recorded the highest number of fatalities and Telangana most heatwaves, junior home minister Nityanand Rai said. Delhi reported 32 heatstroke cases and no deaths.Rai stated MHA has, acting on the recommendations of the 16th Finance Commission, included heatwave and lightning in the list of notified natural calamities under the operational guidelines for administration of SDRF and NDRF for the 2026-31 award period.He added that a policy framework for providing relief assistance through SDRF and NDRF is now in place.
Article Summary: 4,853 cases of heatstroke were reported across country since March 1 this year. Maharashtra recorded the highest number of fatalities and Telangana most heatwaves. Delhi reported 32 heatstroke cases and no deaths. MHA has included heatwave and lightning in the list of notified natural calamities.

Article Title: 274 fugitives brought back from 36 nations since 2019
Article Text:
Union minister Amit Shah has emphasised a three-pronged strategy against fugitives — global outreach, strong coordination and smart diplomacy, MHA said

NEW DEHI: Modi govt brought back 274 fugitives - wanted in cases related to terror, organised crime, murder and economic offences, among other crimes - from 36 countries between 2019 and 2026, besides attaching fugitives' assets worth Rs 17,874 crore over the same period.Ministry of home affairs Tuesday contrasted these statistics with the record of UPA govt, which had no dedicated law to deal with economic fugitives or to confiscate their assets."Between 2004 and 2013, India secured extradition of only four fugitives per year... while 110 extradition requests remained pending," said an MHA spokesperson, adding extradition agreements existed with only 37 countries then, with incomplete documentation and slow processing making the extradition process highly cumbersome.Stating Modi govt treats extradition of fugitives as a "national priority", MHA said the turnaround since 2019 has focused on updating legal and institutional frameworks, sustained diplomatic persistence and continuous follow-up on extradition requests by agencies. "Union minister Amit Shah has emphasised a three-pronged strategy against fugitives - global outreach, strong coordination and smart diplomacy," MHA said in the statement.This is reflected in the figures: 274 fugitives - including 26/11 attacks conspirator Tahawwur Hussain Rana, who was extradited from the US - have been brought back to India since 2019 and 541 Interpol red corner notices issued between 2022 and 2026.The strengthening of the legal framework against fugitives started in 2019-20 with amendments to NIA Act and UAPA law to expand the scope of action to individual terrorists and funding networks abroad. The new criminal laws implemented in 2024 provide for 'trial in absentia' of the fugitive accused.Besides, strict enforcement of PMLA ensured the attachment of assets worth Rs 17,874 crore between 2019 and 2026, with restitution of funds to the tune of Rs 18,762 crore.Govt on Tuesday said these efforts reflect a "whole of govt" approach, with central and state agencies working in close coordination to ensure the return of fugitive offenders and deliver speedy justice to victims.
Article Summary: Modi govt brought back 274 fugitives - wanted in cases related to terror, organised crime, murder and economic offences, among other crimes - from 36 countries between 2019 and 2026, besides attaching fugitives' assets worth Rs 17,874 crore over the same period. UPA govt had no dedicated law to deal with economic fugitives or to confiscate their assets.
